primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Holt-Oram syndrome due to TBX5 haploinsufficiency
mechanism: TBX5 encodes a T-box transcription factor required for coordinated development of the upper limbs and heart. Haploinsufficiency disrupts radial-ray development and cardiac septation/conduction, producing the characteristic heart-hand phenotype.
vignette: A 7-year-old girl has a hypoplastic left thumb and shortened radius. Echocardiography shows a secundum atrial septal defect, and ECG demonstrates first-degree atrioventricular block. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous loss-of-function variant in TBX5.
lead: Which of the following best describes the normal function of the affected gene product?
correct: A transcription factor coordinating upper-limb development and cardiac septation/conduction
distractors: A structural extracellular-matrix protein that provides elastic recoil to the aortic wall
A transcription factor involved in pharyngeal-arch and conotruncal development
A gap-junction protein that electrically couples ventricular cardiomyocytes
A receptor in the Notch signaling pathway required for bile-duct and pulmonary-artery development
distractor_notes: Fibrillin-1 is an extracellular-matrix protein involved in Marfan syndrome and does not explain the radial-ray/ASD phenotype.
TBX1-related pharyngeal-arch developmental defects are associated with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome and conotruncal anomalies, not classic Holt-Oram heart-hand syndrome.
Connexins participate in electrical coupling but do not account for the combined radial-ray and cardiac septation phenotype caused by TBX5 loss.
JAG1/NOTCH2 signaling defects are associated with Alagille syndrome rather than Holt-Oram syndrome.
key_expl: Holt-Oram syndrome is caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in TBX5. TBX5 is a T-box transcription factor involved in upper-limb and cardiac development. Loss of one functional copy produces preaxial radial-ray abnormalities together with septal defects and/or progressive conduction disease.
objective: Identify TBX5 as the developmental transcription factor linking radial-ray abnormalities with cardiac septation and conduction disease in Holt-Oram syndrome.
